name: Generate-And-Filter
description: A generator surveys the brief, fans out one candidate execution context per approach at runtime, and a pre-declared filter picks the winner from every candidate's structured output.

charter.mission: Choose one implementation approach by building every plausible candidate independently and selecting the winner on evidence, not on argument. The generator decides HOW MANY candidates the problem deserves at runtime; the filter is authored up front so the fan-out always converges somewhere the planner chose.
conventions: Each candidate is a self-contained attempt at the brief: it may read shared context, but it never reads or edits another candidate's work.
A candidate reports its own score honestly, including a low one. The filter is the judge; a candidate that inflates its score only makes the filter's job harder.
nonGoals: Merging two candidates into a hybrid — the filter picks one and says why.
Expanding a second time from a candidate: expansion authority stops at the generator, so the fan-out is one level deep by construction.

invariants.statement: No candidate context reads, edits, or depends on another candidate's output. Each is an independent attempt at the same brief, so the filter compares like with like.
Every context the generator creates carries an edge into context-filter. A candidate with no path to the filter is work nobody will read.

sourcesOfTruth.label: Candidate brief
sourcesOfTruth.description: The problem statement every candidate implements and the filter judges against: what has to be true of a solution, and what the tradeoff axes are.

sourcesOfTruth.label: Repository engineering contract
sourcesOfTruth.description: The engineering contract every candidate's implementation has to satisfy — typing, testing, and architecture boundaries.

executionContexts.title: Survey the brief and fan out candidates
executionContexts.description: Read the candidate brief, decide which distinct approaches are worth building, and create one execution context per approach.
executionContexts.acceptanceCriteria: The brief has been read and a set of genuinely distinct approaches chosen, with a one-line reason for each. One execution context per approach exists in the running graph, each carrying its own build task and an edge into context-filter. The captured output names the approaches and the requestId the expansion was submitted under.

outputSchema.description: What the generator decided, so the filter and the audit trail can both read it.

approaches.description: The approaches fanned out, in the order the candidates were created.

expansionRequestId.description: The single-use idempotency key the expansion was submitted under.

executionContexts.title: Filter to the winning candidate
executionContexts.description: Compare every candidate's reported result against the brief and pick exactly one winner.
executionContexts.acceptanceCriteria: Every candidate that ran has been considered — none silently dropped — and exactly one is chosen, with a rationale that cites the brief's tradeoff axes rather than restating the scores. The captured output names the winning context id.

chosenContextId.description: The execution context id of the winning candidate.

rationale.description: Why this candidate wins, in the brief's own terms.

tasks.title: Choose the approaches and expand the graph
Pick the winning candidate
tasks.instructions:
Every candidate's result is in the "Inputs from upstream" section of this prompt as validated structured output — read `approach` and `score` by field rather than re-deriving them, and read the generator's own output for the approach list it intended.

Compare each candidate against the brief's tradeoff axes, not against each other's scores: a candidate that scored itself generously is still only as good as what it built. Consider every candidate that ran; if one looks unfinished, say so rather than dropping it silently.

Choose exactly one winner and complete this task with a summary naming the winning context id and why it wins in the brief's terms.
